### Exact nonzero spectral quotient construction

Current proof target is the literal Hilbert quotient by actual derivative
history, with every nonzero generalized root space and algebraic multiplicity
preserved. For a nonzero scalar `lam`, the certified spectrum `{0}` makes
`B|R - lam I` invertible. The quotient map intertwines shifted powers. If a
quotient vector is killed by the `n`th shifted power, lift it to `x`; that power
of `x` lies in `R`. Invert the same power on `R` and subtract its preimage.
The corrected lift belongs to the full `n`th root space. Intersection with `R`
is zero by invertibility, so the lift is unique. This proves an exact linear
equivalence for every finite root level and their maximal union, hence the
same algebraic multiplicity used by the existing determinant theorem.

admitted at this single weight. Finite complex linear combinations are
admitted and belong to the actual closed derivative submodule, because
their `toLp` classes are the corresponding finite sums of actual shift
classes. The submodule quotient kills each such sum. Apply the same

including the empty prime alphabet. A singleton prime word is in that
squarefree alphabet, so this weight admits every individual prime letter
and the entire Euler word simultaneously. No nonzero-coefficient or
source-admission premise is needed.

Dependency-closed paper mechanism: for fixed Schwartz `psi`, the exact
Leibniz expansion of a modulated `n`th jet is a finite sum with wave
coefficients `(−i*a)^j`, `j≤n`, times original `psi` jets. Weighted
pointwise bounds give seminorm bounds. For finite `s`, put `K` equal to
the largest derivative order in `s`; sum the nonnegative finite Leibniz
seminorm constants to obtain `C_s`. Then
`norm(J_s(modulation_a(psi))) ≤ C_s*(1+a^2)^K`, since
`|a|^j ≤ (1+a^2)^K` for `j≤K`. The empty-product case gives zero.
The implementation now targets the sharper explicit finite-sum majorant
`sum_(k,n)∈s sum_j≤n choose(n,j)*|a|^j*p_(k,n−j)(psi)` directly.
After multiplication by `norm(F_phys(phi)(a))`, every summand is integrable
by the installed actual Schwartz polynomial-norm integrability theorem;
finite summation proves the full majorant integrable. This removes the
auxiliary smooth polynomial and maximum-degree estimate without adding an
assumption. Actual modulation continuity gives strong measurability.
Coordinate evaluation commutes with this genuine Banach
integral. The scalar inverse formula applied to every actual spatial
jet of `phi` identifies its moments; full Leibniz identifies their finite
sum with `J_s(psi*phi)`. Thus the exact Banach integral is
`2*pi • J_s(psi*phi)`. For actual arbitrary `Q`, the already-derived
factorization `Q=L∘J_s` allows genuine Banach integral commutation and
gives `Q(psi*phi)=(1/(2*pi))*integral(F_phys(phi)(a)*Q(modulation_a(psi)),a)`.

Paper mechanism to audit: the installed `cutoffScaled R` is one on
`|x|≤R`, supported in `|x|≤2R`, and has `j`th derivative bounded by
`B_j/R^j`, with `B_j` a proved bound on the fixed smooth compact profile.
Full Leibniz expands the actual difference. Its `j=0` term vanishes on
`|x|<R`; outside, the extra original spatial weight gives
`|x|^k*norm(psi^(n)(x))≤p_(k+1,n)(psi)/R`. For each `j≥1`, `R≥1`
gives `R^(-j)≤R^(-1)` and the original `p_(k,n−j)(psi)` controls
the remaining weighted derivative. The finite binomial sum is therefore
`C_(k,n,psi)/R`. Every original seminorm tends to zero for `R=N+1`,
so the actual installed Schwartz topology gives convergence. A compact
wave test times actual `psi` is exactly the cutoff of its actual modulation.
The multiplier-kernel premise annihilates every such product; continuity
and actual Schwartz convergence give all real modulation probes. Conversely,
the now-proved full correlation formula gives the entire actual product
kernel from those probes. Actual physical Fourier transport and the already
proved original theta derivative/translation annihilator equivalence give
the full Xi-kernel identity. No bare wave is inserted into Schwartz, and no
assumed approximation, inverse-integral interchange or artificial norm is used.

Paper mechanism before new Lean code: the real Xi zero set is closed because
the actual Schwartz symbol is continuous. At each member the certified actual
isolating-radius theorem makes the relative zero set discrete. Intersecting
with any compact set is therefore compact and discrete, hence finite. For
compact phi let W be exactly the zeros in tsupport(phi), and set
R=phi-sum_(z in W)(chi_z*phi), using the original continuous Schwartz
multiplication maps and already constructed compact isolating cutoffs.
Each product and the finite sum are compact; every product support is inside
tsupport(phi), so tsupport(R) is too. At t in W, chi_t has germ one; for
z!=t, if t belonged to tsupport(chi_z), Xi(t)=0 and isolation would force
t=z. Thus each such chi_z has germ zero at t. Intersect the finitely many
neighborhoods to obtain R=0 near t. Every Xi zero in tsupport(R) would belong
to W, contradicted by that germ. Certified compact division implies Q(R)=0
for original Xi*Q=0. Original linearity and exact localizer evaluation then
give Q(phi)=sum_(z in W)(thetaXiTemperedLocalization z Q)(phi).

Dependency-closed PAPER mechanism for compact density: fix a genuine smooth
compact complex cutoff chi equal to1 on the real unit ball. For real R>=1,
use chi(x/R)*phi(x). This is an actual compact Schwartz test. The cutoff
error and every positive-order cutoff derivative vanish inside |x|<R.
Outside that ball, the ORIGINAL (k+1,n) seminorm gives
|x|^k*|D^n phi(x)| <= seminorm(k+1,n,phi)/R. The genuine chain rule scales

### Literal two-Gaussian comparison: exact paper closure and Lean work queue

The closing comparison is part of this whole-card audit. Its source is
EXACTLY k(x)=exp(-x²)+exp(-2x²), not an unspecified Gaussian mixture or
postulated Jordan family. The original comparison claims positivity,
evenness, strict log-concavity, off-real Fourier zeros and the same ordinary
derivative zero-Jordan history. Its proof is separated below into exact
unconditional obligations. No compactness or Hilbert--Schmidt hypothesis
for this Gaussian inverse is added to the comparison.

- [x] G1: construct the literal PositiveDensitySource, its mass and
  positivity/evenness; prove strict concavity of its actual logarithm.
- [x] G2: identify its literal complex-frequency Lebesgue Fourier integral
  at EVERY z, its entire closed formula, positivity on the real line and
  an explicit non-real zero.
- [ ] G3: admit EVERY ordinary derivative to ORIGINAL L²(k⁻¹ dx), prove
  their full linear independence, and identify the actual pinned source
  primitive on EVERY derivative, yielding the genuine full and centered
  zero-Jordan chains through the actual quantile unitary.
- [ ] Run exact leaf native/literal/public/native-API/axiom/index/lint
  gates, reconcile the whole-card certificate and fresh recursive census.

Dependency-closed G1 proof. Set u=x² and g=exp(-u)>0. Then k=g+g²,
k'=-2xg-4xg² and k''=(4u-2)g+(16u-4)g². Exact expansion gives

    (k')²-k k'' = 2g² [1+(3-2u)g+2g²].

Real.add_one_le_exp at u/2, squaring nonnegative sides and using
exp(u)=exp(u/2)², gives exp(u)≥(1+u/2)²≥2u. Multiplication by
g and exp(u)g=1 gives 2u g≤1. Thus the bracket is at least
3g+2g²>0. Actual (log k)''=(k k''-(k')²)/k²<0 everywhere,
which gives StrictConcaveOn ℝ univ (log ∘ k) by the one-dimensional
second-derivative criterion. Continuity/positivity/evenness are direct;
Gaussian integrability gives a literal source with mass
sqrt(π)+sqrt(π/2)>0.

Dependency-closed G2 proof. The actual complex quadratic Gaussian integral
applied with quadratic coefficient -1 or -2 and linear coefficient iz
gives, for EVERY z∈ℂ,

    ∫ exp(izx) k(x) dx
      = A exp(-z²/4)+B exp(-z²/8),
    A=sqrt(π)>0, B=sqrt(π/2)>0.

Each integrand is genuinely integrable at every complex frequency, by
the same quadratic Gaussian integrability theorem. Real positive square
root and complex half-power identities fix these exact constants.
The displayed formula is entire and is strictly positive for real z.
Let c=B/A>0, w=-8(log c+iπ), and take the literal principal complex
half-power z=w^(1/2). The unconditional complex natural-multiple power
identity gives z²=w. Hence exp(-z²/8)=-c and
exp(-z²/4)=c², so the Fourier integral is Ac²-Bc=0.
Im(w)=-8π≠0 forces Im(z)≠0. This uses no numerical root or RH premise.

Dependency-closed G3 proof. For b=1,2, define polynomial P_b,0=1 and
P_b,n+1=P_b,n'-2b X P_b,n. Repeated actual differentiation gives
D^n exp(-bx²)=P_b,n(x) exp(-bx²), with degree n and leading
coefficient (-2b)^n. Since k≥exp(-x²) and exp(-2x²)≤exp(-x²),
the squared absolute value of EVERY D^n k divided by k is dominated
by a constant times (1+|x|)^(2n) exp(-x²), genuinely integrable.
All these jets are continuous, integrable in Lebesgue measure and tend
to zero at BOTH ends. Thus, for EVERY n,

    ∫ D^(n+1) k = 0,
    ∫_{-∞}^x D^(n+1) k = D^n k(x).

The actual pinned primitive
i∫_{-∞}^x [f-(∫f/M)k] therefore kills k and sends D^(n+1) k
to i D^n k pointwise. These are equalities of genuinely admitted source
classes after quotienting by almost-everywhere equality, then transport
through the actual source quantile isometry. Full independence follows
without an assumed Jordan basis: any finite relation is
P(x)+exp(-x²)Q(x)=0 after dividing by exp(-x²). Its polynomial P
tends to zero at +∞, so P=0. Highest-degree coefficient of P is the
highest nonzero relation coefficient times (-2)^n; this contradiction
kills every coefficient. Actual weighted a.e. equality gives pointwise
equality by continuity and the strictly positive density. For n≥1,
integral zero makes the transported derivative orthogonal to the actual
constant vector. Orthogonal removal thus kills the first centered jet
and lowers every later centered jet by i. No asserted global bounded
Gaussian inverse or finite-kernel-energy assumption is used in this
chain comparison.

# FZZ literal worldsheet replica genus/cycle transport

- **ID:** FZZ-LITERAL-GENUS-CYCLE-TRANSPORT
- **Stage:** 5-failed
- **Type:** FALSIFIED
- **Statement:** Literal replica topology transports fixed-genus homology-cycle data to a nonzero first replica tangent.

## Exact kill

At physical `k>3`, continued genus `g(delta)=(1-1/(k-2))delta` is fractional for `0<delta<=1`. Every continuous literal `Nat`-genus family is locally constant, so every genus/cycle observable has zero derivative; required genus and exact loop/divisor-charge tangents are strictly positive.

## Positive survivor

Fixed-genus two-cycle selector still characterizes the critical line. Only analytic continuation of full correlators/moduli beyond literal topology can transport it into replica response.

## Lean

`RHTower.fzzCigarParity_worldsheetReplicaGenusContinuation_noGo` in `GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.FZZCigarParityWorldsheetReplicaGenusContinuationNoGo`; targeted build PASS; standard axioms only.

# Route U — owned factual results

- On every positive moment block through degree `n + 2`, Gaussian-visible Jacobi energy at
  degree `n` is bounded by the completed nondegenerate source history at `n + 1`, with the
  exact quadratic effectivity weight `(2n + 1)^2 + 2`.
- On every actual shifted-Xi positive block through `n + 3`, next canonical admission norm times
  current literal Gaussian bulk is at most next literal adjacent arithmetic source supply.
- Normalized relative Gaussian bulk equals `w^4` times the actual completed-square visible
  energy on a positive block through `n + 4`; this transports the shifted alpha square and all
  beta terms, not an unshifted surrogate.
- Consequently, on every sufficiently far-right positive block through `n + 4` with `n ≥ 2`,
  literal adjacent source supply satisfies
  `N_n N_(n+1) / 4 < w^4 * routeUAdjacentLiteralSourceSupply(w, n + 1)`.
- Exact gauge law: `normalizedAdmissionNorm(w,n) = (2w/log w) w^(4n) N_n` on every actual
  positive block.  Thus raw consecutive norm collapse is a completely determined mass-density
  factor, not an independent sparse-escape mechanism.
- Consequently, on every sufficiently far-right positive block through `n + 4` with `n ≥ 2`,
  `log(w)^2 * normalizedAdmissionNorm(w,n) * normalizedAdmissionNorm(w,n+1) <
  16 * w^(8n+10) * routeUAdjacentLiteralSourceSupply(w,n+1)`.
- The retained Route U obstruction is exact: prove a finite source-faithful upper ceiling for
  the mass-scaled literal supply on the right-hand side.  This is the Route-U shadow required of

## 6. Bold field conjecture

### Conjecture CJFM-A -- source formation comparisons preserve the canonical positive refinement

Source Formation Harmonic Mechanics already constructs one literal pre-zero Moebius source with
coherent execution, positive variation, recurrence/open history, hypertranscendental rank, and
bilateral radial selection. The open conjecture is therefore narrower and harder: there exist
coefficient-faithful comparison maps from that same positive refinement to at least four
structurally different organs, preserving composition and reserve before observer reduction. Their
current no-gos should then be failures of those reductions to retain reserve.

The conjecture is stronger than a common categorical container. It predicts a shared positive
quantity and compatible composition law, not merely functors into a common category.

### Falsifier

Exhibit two route realizations for which every source-natural candidate positive refinement either:

1. depends on the target zero;
2. fails composition;
3. is not preserved by source equivalence;
4. reduces to endpoint data; or
5. assigns incompatible reserve to one shared source intervention.

## 7. First open theorem

Construct the comparison from the existing literal Euler/Moebius source refinement before Mellin
or Xi specialization. It must simultaneously map to:

1. centered generative tangent;
2. causal drift history;
3. positive Gram birth;
4. prime-log recurrence history.

Then prove one joint reconstruction or conservation identity. Only after that may a fifth organ be
predicted or an RH selection theorem attempted.

## 8. Why existing attacks do not kill this conjecture yet

- **Common-recovery flatness:** acts after signed reduction; CJFM retains pre-recovery legs.
- **Radial-gauge blindness:** diagonal total-grade-one observer sees `D`; CJFM asks for the two
  source-generated polarities before diagonal cancellation.
- **Information neutrality:** expected; endpoint information is deliberately a quotient invariant.
- **Zero-delay gauge:** absolute delay is discarded. Reserve is the translation-invariant excess
  `Lambda-|D|`.
- **Positive phase loss:** scalar positive norms may erase orientation, but a polarized pair retains
  which leg was generated before the phase quotient.
- **HT not equal noncompactness:** CJFM predicts reserve growth in prolongation depth, not HT as a
  topological slogan.

These observations show only that the representation survives known attacks. They do not prove the
source refinement exists.

## 9. Kill conditions

Retire this field candidate if:

1. no literal pre-zero source operation produces both legs;
2. the pair is an arbitrary Hahn/Jordan decomposition chosen after observer reduction;
3. composition cannot be made source-natural;
4. all route shadows require unrelated reserve functionals;
5. no theorem in a fourth organ follows from three realized organs; or
6. properness/passivity is equivalent to RH when stated at source level.

## 10. Literature boundary

Jordan decomposition, ordered vector spaces, Titchmarsh convolution support, causal convolution
algebras, total variation, Markov recovery, and data processing are established. Formation Holonomy
Mechanics already supplies an abstract vertical-fibre grammar.

Source Formation Harmonic Mechanics supplies the literal positive/coherent source side. The proposed
field delta is therefore its source-generated coupling to causal and recovery doctrines:

\[
 \text{positive refinement}
 \longrightarrow
 \text{causal formation}
 \longrightarrow
 \text{signed observer/recovery quotient},
\]

with functional-equation polarity exchange and a proper reserve law. Until a literal multi-organ
source functor is constructed, this remains a Stage-1 programme rather than a new field claim.

def suzukiCompactSmoothPositiveL2
    (g : ℝ → ℂ) (hsmooth : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g)
    (hcompact : HasCompactSupport g) : SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  suzukiPositiveHalfLineUnitary
    (logEvenUnitary.symm (suzukiCompactSmoothLogL2 g hsmooth hcompact))

/-- Literal output vector on Suzuki's positive-half-line carrier. -/
def suzukiCompactSmoothLiteralPositiveHankelL2
    (omega c : ℝ) (homega : 0 < omega) (hc : 1 / 2 + omega < c)
    (hinner : SuzukiCanonicalThetaMeromorphicInner omega)
    (g : ℝ → ℂ) (hsmooth : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g)
    (hcompact : HasCompactSupport g) : SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  suzukiPositiveHalfLineUnitary
    (logEvenUnitary.symm
      (suzukiCompactSmoothLiteralLogHankelL2 omega c homega hc hinner
        g hsmooth hcompact))

/-- The positive-half-line and even-carrier realizations of Suzuki's spectral unitary are exactly
conjugate by the explicit carrier equivalence. -/
theorem suzukiCanonicalPositiveHankelUnitary_positiveHalfLineUnitary
    (omega : ℝ) (hinner : SuzukiCanonicalThetaMeromorphicInner omega)
    (f : evenSubspace) :
    suzukiCanonicalPositiveHankelUnitary omega hinner
        (suzukiPositiveHalfLineUnitary f) =
      suzukiPositiveHalfLineUnitary
        (suzukiCanonicalHankelUnitary omega hinner f) := by
  simp [suzukiCanonicalPositiveHankelUnitary,
    suzukiPositiveShiftedFourierUnitary,
    suzukiCanonicalHankelUnitary,
    suzukiShiftedFourierUnitary,
    suzukiEvenExtension_positiveRestriction]

/-- **Suzuki (2012), Lemma 4.1 on the literal positive-half-line carrier.** -/
theorem suzuki2012_lemma_four_one_positive_half_line_literal_kernel
    {omega c : ℝ} (homega : 0 < omega) (hc : 1 / 2 + omega < c)
    (hinner : SuzukiCanonicalThetaMeromorphicInner omega)
    (g : ℝ → ℂ) (hsmooth : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g)
    (hcompact : HasCompactSupport g) :
    suzukiCanonicalPositiveHankelUnitary omega hinner
        (suzukiCompactSmoothPositiveL2 g hsmooth hcompact) =
      suzukiCompactSmoothLiteralPositiveHankelL2 omega c homega hc hinner
        g hsmooth hcompact := by
  simp only [suzukiCompactSmoothPositiveL2,
    suzukiCompactSmoothLiteralPositiveHankelL2]
  rw [suzukiCanonicalPositiveHankelUnitary_positiveHalfLineUnitary]
  rw [suzuki2012_lemma_four_one_literal_kernel_on_compact_smooth_log_core
    homega hc hinner g hsmooth hcompact]

end

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ThetaCusp.ThetaCuspHawkingBMLaplacePowerJets

/-!
The literal third radial jet of the positive complex power.

The source-pole strip requires a cubic endpoint subtraction.  This is the exact
third jet of the source's existing positive-radius power, with no asymptotic
replacement.
-/

open Complex Set Filter Topology
namespace RHTower.D4BMLaplaceRadial
noncomputable section

attribute [-instance] instInnerProductSpaceRealComplex
attribute [-instance] RCLike.toInnerProductSpaceReal
attribute [-instance] NormedSpace.complexToReal

/-- The literal third positive-radius derivative of the original complex power. -/
def powerThird (a : ℂ) (z : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  a * (a - 1) * (a - 2) * power a z / (z : ℂ) ^ (3 : ℕ)

/-- The third radial jet follows by differentiating the already literal second jet. -/
theorem powerSecond_hasDerivAt (a : ℂ) {z : ℝ} (hz : 0 < z) :
    HasDerivAt (powerSecond a) (powerThird a z) z := by
  have hz0 : (z : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr (ne_of_gt hz)
  have hfirst := (power_derivatives a hz).1
  have hnum := hfirst.const_mul (a * (a - 1))
  have hquot := hnum.div (((hasDerivAt_id z).ofReal_comp).pow 2) (pow_ne_zero 2 hz0)
  apply hquot.congr_deriv
  dsimp [powerSecond, powerThird, powerFirst]
  field_simp [hz0]

/-- All three literal positive-radius derivatives of the original power. -/
theorem power_derivatives_three (a : ℂ) {z : ℝ} (hz : 0 < z) :
    HasDerivAt (power a) (powerFirst a z) z ∧
      HasDerivAt (powerFirst a) (powerSecond a z) z ∧
      HasDerivAt (powerSecond a) (powerThird a z) z :=
  ⟨(power_derivatives a hz).1, (power_derivatives a hz).2,
    powerSecond_hasDerivAt a hz⟩

end
end RHTower.D4BMLaplaceRadial

/-!
# Euler--Wold Jordan admission into the literal Xi conormal co-short

The intrinsic Hahn--Jordan Euler/Wold residuals are admitted componentwise into the actual
four-orientation Route-P conormal short.  No addition or grade-forgetting is performed: the
negative Euler and positive Wold matrices are shortened separately.

The main finite law is stronger than a cofinal matching.  If `S(c)=4‖c‖²` is the literal
four-orientation short and `A₊(c,N)` is the admitted Wold leg, then the existing regularized Xi
endpoint response `R(c,q,N)` satisfies

`A₊(c,N) + R(c,q,N) = 2 S(c)`

at every source clock.  This is the Green--Stokes complement transported through the conormal
short: Wold Jordan mass is twice the interior third jet, while the endpoint response is twice the
same short times the complementary endpoint third jet.

The coefficient is then specialized to the actual multiplicity-split completed-Xi residue.  At
positive aperture it is literally the Gamma--Julia source coupling times Burnol's nested-window
top-conormal feature.  Summation over the actual support fibre restores analytic multiplicity.
No Loewner order, equivariance, spectral projection, scalar contractivity, or RH premise is used.
-/

open scoped BigOperators ComplexOrder

/-- Literal scalar Schur contraction of the physical corner through the retained environment
pivot.  It is a rational matrix operation, not an operator-spectrum construction. -/
def sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort
    (B : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) : ℂ :=
  B 0 0 - B 0 1 * (B 1 1)⁻¹ * B 1 0

/-- Real value of the complete four-orientation conormal short. -/
def sourceHorizontalLiteralConormalShort (c : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  4 * Complex.normSq c

/-- Shorting a real multiple of the diagonal four-orientation orbit retains its sign and exact
coefficient.  This applies to the negative Euler leg as well as the positive Wold leg. -/
theorem sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort_orbit_smul
    (a : ℝ) (c : ℂ) :
    sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort
        (((a : ℂ) • routePJuliaSharedOrientationOrbitBlock c)) =
      (a * sourceHorizontalLiteralConormalShort c : ℝ) := by
  rw [sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort,
    routePJuliaSharedOrientationOrbitBlock_eq_diagonal]
  simp [sourceHorizontalLiteralConormalShort]

/-- The unweighted literal conormal contraction is `4‖c‖²`. -/
theorem sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort_orbit
    (c : ℂ) :
    sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort
        (routePJuliaSharedOrientationOrbitBlock c) =
      (sourceHorizontalLiteralConormalShort c : ℂ) := by
  simpa using sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort_orbit_smul 1 c

/-- Componentwise, unrecompressed conormal admission of the Euler negative and Wold positive
Hahn--Jordan residuals. -/
def sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanConormalAdmission
    (c : ℂ) (N : ℕ) : Fin 2 → ℝ :=
  ![-sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanNegativeMass N *
      sourceHorizontalLiteralConormalShort c,
    sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanPositiveMass N *
      sourceHorizontalLiteralConormalShort c]

/-- Exact finite normalization: positive Hahn--Jordan mass is twice the BV interior third jet. -/
theorem sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanPositiveMass_eq_two_mul_interiorThirdJet
    (N : ℕ) :
    sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanPositiveMass N =
      2 * sourceHorizontalWoldBVGreenStokesInteriorThirdJet N := by
  rw [sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanPositiveMass_eq,
    sourceHorizontalWoldBVGreenStokesInteriorThirdJet,
    sourceHorizontalWoldOrderedNormalizedMoment,
    sourceHorizontalWoldCubicCountertermMoment]
  ring

/-- First admitted component is the literal non-spectral short of the negative Euler action. -/
theorem sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanConormalAdmission_action
    (c : ℂ) (N : ℕ) :
    (sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort
      (sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanSelectedPhysicalAction c N)).re =
        sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanConormalAdmission c N 0 := by
  rw [sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanSelectedPhysicalAction,
    sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort_orbit_smul]
  simp [sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanConormalAdmission]

/-- Second admitted component is the literal non-spectral short of the positive Wold regulator. -/
theorem sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanConormalAdmission_regulator
    (c : ℂ) (N : ℕ) :
    (sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort
      (sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanSelectedRegulator c N)).re =
        sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanConormalAdmission c N 1 := by
  rw [sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanSelectedRegulator,
    sourceHorizontalNonSpectralConormalShort_orbit_smul]
  simp [sourceHorizontalEulerWoldJordanConormalAdmission]

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.CCM.CCMRestrictedWeilPoleBoundaryPrimitives
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.PoleSelfEnergyLimit

/-!
# Eventual positive trace of the literal CCM pole matrix

The actual CCM pole diagonal has the same one-sided Gamma boundary primitive as the
exponential-pole diagonal whose sharp asymptotic is already formalized.  This transfers its
positive genus limit to the literal CCM matrix.  Consequently the large-aperture two-pole
compression cannot have two negative parity energies: once its determinant wall is crossed,
exactly one parity is negative.

This is a trace law only.  It neither controls the off-diagonal entry nor proves the
RH-equivalent determinant inequality.
-/

open Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The actual CCM and exponential-pole self-boundary primitives are definitionally the same
one-sided Gamma integral. -/
theorem ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryPrimitive_eq_poleSelfBoundaryPrimitive (s : ℝ) :
    ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryPrimitive s = poleSelfBoundaryPrimitive s := by
  rfl

/-- The literal CCM pole diagonal is the sharp exponential-pole diagonal at the same aperture. -/
theorem ccmWeilPoleDiagonal_eq_poleDiagonalExplicit (a : SuzukiPositiveAperture) :
    ccmWeilPoleDiagonal a = poleDiagonalExplicit a.1 := by
  rw [ccmWeilPoleDiagonal_eq_error,
    ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryMass_eq_primitive,
    ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryPrimitive_eq_poleSelfBoundaryPrimitive]
  rfl

/-- **Eventual positive trace.**  The trace coordinate of the literal CCM two-pole matrix is
strictly positive beyond one unconditional aperture threshold. -/
theorem exists_eventually_ccmWeilPoleDiagonal_pos :
    ∃ A : ℝ, ∀ a : SuzukiPositiveAperture, A ≤ a.1 →
      0 < ccmWeilPoleDiagonal a := by
  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := eventually_atTop.1 eventually_poleDiagonalExplicit_pos
  refine ⟨A, fun a ha => ?_⟩
  rw [ccmWeilPoleDiagonal_eq_poleDiagonalExplicit]
  exact hA a.1 ha

/-- Above the positive-trace threshold, a strict pole-compression wall crossing has one and only
one negative parity energy.  The other parity remains strictly positive. -/
theorem ccmWeilPoleCompression_parity_opposite_sign_of_diagonal_pos_of_cross_exceeds
    (a : SuzukiPositiveAperture)
    (hdiag : 0 < ccmWeilPoleDiagonal a)
    (hcross : ccmWeilPoleDiagonal a < |ccmWeilPoleCross a|) :
    (ccmRestrictedWeilSourceQuadratic a (ccmPolarParityFormVector a 1) < 0 ∧
      0 < ccmRestrictedWeilSourceQuadratic a (ccmPolarParityFormVector a (-1))) ∨
    (0 < ccmRestrictedWeilSourceQuadratic a (ccmPolarParityFormVector a 1) ∧
      ccmRestrictedWeilSourceQuadratic a (ccmPolarParityFormVector a (-1)) < 0) := by
  rw [ccmWeilPoleCompression_parity_energy a (Or.inl rfl),
    ccmWeilPoleCompression_parity_energy a (Or.inr rfl)]
  rcases le_total 0 (ccmWeilPoleCross a) with hnonneg | hnonpos
  · right
    rw [abs_of_nonneg hnonneg] at hcross
    constructor <;> nlinarith
  · left
    rw [abs_of_nonpos hnonpos] at hcross
    constructor <;> nlinarith

end

end RHTower

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ProlateRescaledProfileBounds
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ProlateHermitePairingHypotheses
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ProlateCanonicalRadialFamily
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ProlateBandEigenMass

/-!
# The signed mode is pinned to the oscillator ladder at rate `1/c`

The canonical radial representative of a live signed mode is an endpoint-normalized band
eigenfunction, hence globally bounded together with its first two derivatives.  Its Hermite
rescaling therefore satisfies every hypothesis of the ladder pin, and the pin reads

```text
|c·s − (2m+1)| · |⟨u, φ_m⟩|  =  |⟨u, W_m⟩| / c ,
```

an identity whose right-hand side carries the full factor `1/c` and involves the profile only
through a bounded pairing against a fixed Gaussian-decaying weight.  So the scaled separation
constant is within `O(1/c)` of every oscillator rung whose Hermite pairing does not vanish.
-/

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Filter

open scoped Topology ContDiff

namespace RHTower

/-- The canonical radial representative of a live signed mode is a global band eigenfunction. -/
theorem bandTransform_signedModeRadialData_R {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (n : ℕ)
    (hvalue : evenProlateSignedValue a n ≠ 0) (x : ℝ) :
    bandTransform (signedModeRadialBandwidth a) (signedModeRadialData a n).R x
      = evenProlateSignedValue a n ^ (2 : ℕ) * (signedModeRadialData a n).R x := by
  have hD := signedModeRadialData_isExact ha n hvalue
  have hRdef : (signedModeRadialData a n).R
      = prolateEndpointNormalize (signedModeRadialData a n).Phi := hD.2.2.2.2.1
  have hband := hD.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  rw [hRdef]
  exact GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.bandTransform_endpointNormalize_eigen hband x

/-- The canonical radial representative is bounded together with its first two derivatives. -/
theorem exists_bound_signedModeRadialData_R {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (n : ℕ)
    (hvalue : evenProlateSignedValue a n ≠ 0) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧
      (∀ x, |(signedModeRadialData a n).R x| ≤ B) ∧
      (∀ x, |deriv (signedModeRadialData a n).R x| ≤ B) ∧
      (∀ x, |deriv (deriv (signedModeRadialData a n).R) x| ≤ B) := by
  have hD := signedModeRadialData_isExact ha n hvalue
  have hsm : ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (signedModeRadialData a n).R :=
    hD.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hcont : Continuous (signedModeRadialData a n).R := hsm.continuous
  have hband := bandTransform_signedModeRadialData_R ha n hvalue
  have hlam : evenProlateSignedValue a n ^ (2 : ℕ) ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hvalue
  obtain ⟨C₀, hC₀0, hC₀⟩ := exists_bound_of_bandTransform_eigen hlam hcont hband
  obtain ⟨C₁, hC₁0, hC₁⟩ := exists_bound_deriv_of_bandTransform_eigen hlam hcont hband
  obtain ⟨C₂, hC₂0, hC₂⟩ := exists_bound_deriv2_of_bandTransform_eigen hlam hcont hband
  refine ⟨max C₀ (max C₁ C₂), le_trans hC₀0 (le_max_left _ _), fun x => ?_, fun x => ?_,
    fun x => ?_⟩
  · exact le_trans (hC₀ x) (le_max_left _ _)
  · exact le_trans (hC₁ x) (le_trans (le_max_left _ _) (le_max_right _ _))
  · exact le_trans (hC₂ x) (le_trans (le_max_right _ _) (le_max_right _ _))

/-- The Hermite rescaling of the canonical radial representative. -/
def signedModeRescaledProfile (a : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  prolateHermiteRescale (signedModeRadialBandwidth a) (signedModeRadialData a n).R

theorem signedModeRadialBandwidth_pos {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    0 < signedModeRadialBandwidth a := by
  rw [signedModeRadialBandwidth]
  positivity

/-- **The rescaled signed mode is pinned to every oscillator rung it pairs with.** -/
theorem exists_bound_abs_signedMode_scaledSeparation_sub_rung {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (n : ℕ)
    (hvalue : evenProlateSignedValue a n ≠ 0) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ m : ℕ,
      (∫ x, signedModeRescaledProfile a n x * hermiteFun m x) ≠ 0 →
      |signedModeRadialBandwidth a * (signedModeRadialData a n).s - (2 * m + 1)|
        ≤ B * (∫ x, |prolateDefectWeight m x|)
            / (signedModeRadialBandwidth a
                * |∫ x, signedModeRescaledProfile a n x * hermiteFun m x|) := by
  classical
  have hc : 0 < signedModeRadialBandwidth a := signedModeRadialBandwidth_pos ha
  set c : ℝ := signedModeRadialBandwidth a with hcdef
  have hcne : c ≠ 0 := hc.ne'
  have hsc : 0 < Real.sqrt c := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hc
  set R : ℝ → ℝ := (signedModeRadialData a n).R with hRdef
  have hD := signedModeRadialData_isExact ha n hvalue
  have hsm : ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) R := hD.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have heig : ∀ x : ℝ, prolateSLAction c R x = (signedModeRadialData a n).chi * R x :=
    hD.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hs : (signedModeRadialData a n).s
      = radialSeparationRatio c (signedModeRadialData a n).chi :=
    hD.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  obtain ⟨B, hB0, hBR, hBR', hBR''⟩ := exists_bound_signedModeRadialData_R ha n hvalue
  have hdiff : Differentiable ℝ R := (contDiff_infty_iff_deriv.mp hsm).1
  have hsmd : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (deriv R) := (contDiff_infty_iff_deriv.mp hsm).2
  have hdiff2 : Differentiable ℝ (deriv R) := (contDiff_infty_iff_deriv.mp hsmd).1

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.RiemannGaussian.FiniteToEntireHeatFrontier
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.RiemannGaussian.RiemannXiHyperbolicHeatWindow
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Field.Lemmas

/-!
# Zero-free logarithmic-derivative convergence

This file proves the analytic prerequisite for transporting finite root
divisors to spectral xi.  Locally uniform convergence of holomorphic
functions gives locally uniform convergence of their logarithmic derivatives
on every open region where the limiting function has no zero.  It is then
applied to the exact separable, root-pinned polynomial sequence forced by
failure of RH.

No passage through a limiting zero is asserted here.  Multiplicity-preserving
zero-count stability across a zero-free boundary is the next step.
-/

open Complex Filter Metric Polynomial Set
open scoped Topology

namespace RiemannGaussian

noncomputable section

/-- Locally uniform holomorphic convergence passes to logarithmic
derivatives on every zero-free open region. -/
theorem logDeriv_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
    {ι : Type*} {phi : Filter ι} [phi.NeBot]
    {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    (hF : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F f phi U)
    (hhol : ∀ᶠ n in phi, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F n) U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hzero : ∀ w ∈ U, f w ≠ 0) :
    TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n ↦ logDeriv (F n)) (logDeriv f) phi U := by
  have hfdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U :=
    hF.differentiableOn hhol hU
  have hderiv := hF.deriv hhol hU
  have hquotient := hderiv.div₀ hF
    (hfdiff.deriv hU).continuousOn hfdiff.continuousOn hzero
  refine (hquotient.congr
    (G := fun n ↦ logDeriv (F n)) ?_).congr_right ?_
  · intro n w _
    rfl
  · intro w _
    rfl

/-- On a compact subset where the limit has no zero, all sufficiently late
approximants are themselves zero-free. -/
theorem eventually_forall_ne_zero_on_compact_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
    {ι : Type*} {phi : Filter ι}
    {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U K : Set ℂ}
    (hF : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F f phi U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hK : IsCompact K) (hKU : K ⊆ U)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f U) (hzero : ∀ w ∈ U, f w ≠ 0) :
    ∀ᶠ n in phi, ∀ w ∈ K, F n w ≠ 0 := by
  have hnormContinuous : ContinuousOn (fun w ↦ ‖f w‖) K :=
    continuous_norm.comp_continuousOn (hf.mono hKU)
  have hnormPos : ∀ w ∈ K, 0 < ‖f w‖ := by
    intro w hw
    exact norm_pos_iff.mpr (hzero w (hKU hw))
  obtain ⟨delta, hdelta, hdeltaLe⟩ :=
    hK.exists_forall_le' hnormContinuous hnormPos
  have hUniform :=
    (tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_forall_isCompact hU).mp hF K hKU hK
  rw [Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff] at hUniform
  filter_upwards [hUniform delta hdelta] with n hn
  intro w hw hFn
  have hdist := hn w hw
  rw [hFn, dist_zero_right] at hdist
  exact (not_lt_of_ge (hdeltaLe w hw)) hdist

/-- The approximant logarithmic derivatives are eventually continuous on
every compact zero-free subset. -/
theorem eventually_logDeriv_continuousOn_compact
    {ι : Type*} {phi : Filter ι} [phi.NeBot]
    {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U K : Set ℂ}
    (hF : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F f phi U)
    (hhol : ∀ᶠ n in phi, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F n) U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hK : IsCompact K) (hKU : K ⊆ U)
    (hzero : ∀ w ∈ U, f w ≠ 0) :
    ∀ᶠ n in phi, ContinuousOn (logDeriv (F n)) K := by
  have hfdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U :=
    hF.differentiableOn hhol hU
  have hFnzero :=
    eventually_forall_ne_zero_on_compact_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      hF hU hK hKU hfdiff.continuousOn hzero
  filter_upwards [hhol, hFnzero] with n hnDiff hnZero
  have hderivContinuous : ContinuousOn (deriv (F n)) K :=
    (hnDiff.deriv hU).continuousOn.mono hKU
  have hfunctionContinuous : ContinuousOn (F n) K :=
    hnDiff.continuousOn.mono hKU
  unfold logDeriv
  exact (hderivContinuous.div₀ hfunctionContinuous hnZero).congr
    fun _ _ ↦ rfl

/-- Logarithmic-derivative circle integrals converge across any compact
circle contained in a zero-free open region. -/
theorem tendsto_circleIntegral_logDeriv_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
    {ι : Type*} {phi : Filter ι} [phi.NeBot] [phi.IsCountablyGenerated]
    {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    (hF : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F f phi U)
    (hhol : ∀ᶠ n in phi, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F n) U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hzero : ∀ w ∈ U, f w ≠ 0)
    (c : ℂ) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hsphere : sphere c R ⊆ U) :
    Tendsto
      (fun n ↦ ∮ w in C(c, R), logDeriv (F n) w) phi
      (nhds (∮ w in C(c, R), logDeriv f w)) := by
  have hlog := logDeriv_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn hF hhol hU hzero
  have hUniform :=
    (tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_forall_isCompact hU).mp
      hlog (sphere c R) hsphere (isCompact_sphere c R)
  have hcontinuous := eventually_logDeriv_continuousOn_compact
    hF hhol hU (isCompact_sphere c R) hsphere hzero
  exact hUniform.tendsto_circleIntegral_of_continuousOn hR hcontinuous

/-- Polynomial specialization of zero-free logarithmic-derivative
convergence. -/
theorem realPolynomial_logDeriv_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Hedenmalm.HedenmalmShiftedSourceEquation
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Hedenmalm.HedenmalmThetaZeroHistoryNoGo
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ThetaPowerWeightedDerivativeHistory
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ThetaCusp.ThetaCuspFullDerivativeExponentialMoments

/-!
# Actual theta derivatives and both zero-Jordan chains

The literal complete-source derivatives belong to `L²(k⁻¹ dx)`. Their Lebesgue
integrals and two-ended limits identify their pinned primitives exactly. The
actual quantile inverse lowers this derivative family with coefficient `i`.
Orthogonal scalar removal retains a second infinite Jordan chain, dense range,
and an injective adjoint, obstructing every bounded injective symmetrizer.
The full and centered families are linearly independent; the full closed
history is invariant under the actual compact source inverse.
-/

open MeasureTheory Filter Set Topology Complex

namespace RHTower.HedenmalmThetaSource

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry HedenmalmQuantile HedenmalmHilbertSchmidt
  HedenmalmClosedWeightedDerivative

noncomputable section

attribute [local instance 2000] Real.measurableSpace
attribute [local instance 2000] NormedSpace.complexToReal

private abbrev H := Lp ℂ 2 unitIntervalMeasure
private abbrev HS := SourceSpace thetaSource
private abbrev μS := volume.withDensity (realDensity (sourceWeight thetaSource))

local instance : Fact ((2 : ENNReal) ≠ ⊤) := ⟨by norm_num⟩

/-- The literal ordinary derivative, in complex source coordinates. -/
def thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  ((iteratedDeriv n thetaCuspFullSource x : ℝ) : ℂ)

theorem continuous_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n : ℕ) :
    Continuous (thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n) :=
  Complex.continuous_ofReal.comp
    (contDiff_thetaCuspFullSource.continuous_iteratedDeriv n
      (by exact_mod_cast (ENat.coe_lt_top n).le))

theorem hasDerivAt_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n) (thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n + 1) x) x := by
  change HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => ((iteratedDeriv n thetaCuspFullSource y : ℝ) : ℂ))
    ((iteratedDeriv (n + 1) thetaCuspFullSource x : ℝ) : ℂ) x
  have h := (contDiff_thetaCuspFullSource.differentiable_iteratedDeriv n
    (by exact_mod_cast (ENat.coe_lt_top n)) x).hasDerivAt
  simpa only [← iteratedDeriv_succ] using h.ofReal_comp

theorem integrable_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n) := by
  apply (integrable_norm_iff (continuous_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n).aestronglyMeasurable).mp
  simpa [thetaSourceDerivativeFunction, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs] using
    integrable_exp_abs_mul_abs_iteratedDeriv_thetaCuspFullSource n 0

theorem thetaSourceDerivativeFunction_tendsto_atBot (n : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n) atBot (𝓝 0) := by
  rw [tendsto_zero_iff_norm_tendsto_zero]
  have hb : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atBot,
      ‖thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n x‖ ≤
        finitePrimeThetaCuspWeightedDerivativeConstant n 0 * Real.exp x := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_le_atBot (0 : ℝ)] with x hx
    simpa [thetaSourceDerivativeFunction, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_nonpos hx] using exp_abs_mul_abs_iteratedDeriv_thetaCuspFullSource_le n 0 0 x
  exact squeeze_zero' (Eventually.of_forall fun x => norm_nonneg _) hb
    (by simpa using (Real.tendsto_exp_atBot.const_mul
      (finitePrimeThetaCuspWeightedDerivativeConstant n 0)))

theorem thetaSourceDerivativeFunction_tendsto_atTop (n : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  rw [tendsto_zero_iff_norm_tendsto_zero]
  have hb : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
      ‖thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n x‖ ≤
        finitePrimeThetaCuspWeightedDerivativeConstant n 0 * Real.exp (-x) := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (0 : ℝ)] with x hx
    simpa [thetaSourceDerivativeFunction, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_nonneg hx] using exp_abs_mul_abs_iteratedDeriv_thetaCuspFullSource_le n 0 0 x
  exact squeeze_zero' (Eventually.of_forall fun x => norm_nonneg _) hb
    (by simpa using (Real.tendsto_exp_neg_atTop_nhds_zero.const_mul
      (finitePrimeThetaCuspWeightedDerivativeConstant n 0)))

theorem integral_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction_succ (n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x, thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n + 1) x) = 0 :=
  integral_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrable
    (hasDerivAt_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n)
    (integrable_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n + 1))
    (integrable_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n)

theorem integral_Iic_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction_succ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    (∫ y in Iic x, thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n + 1) y) =
      thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n x := by
  simpa using integral_Iic_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto'
    (fun y _ => hasDerivAt_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction n y)
    (integrable_thetaSourceDerivativeFunction (n + 1)).integrableOn
    (thetaSourceDerivativeFunction_tendsto_atBot n)

/-- Polynomial specialization of zero-free logarithmic-derivative
convergence. -/
theorem realPolynomial_logDeriv_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
    {ι : Type*} {phi : Filter ι} [phi.NeBot]
    (A : ι → ℝ[X]) {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    (hA : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n w ↦ ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval w) f phi U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hzero : ∀ w ∈ U, f w ≠ 0) :
    TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n ↦ logDeriv
        (fun w ↦ ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval w))
      (logDeriv f) phi U := by
  exact logDeriv_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn hA
    (Eventually.of_forall fun n ↦
      ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).differentiableOn)
    hU hzero

/-- Circle-integral specialization for a locally uniformly convergent
sequence of real polynomials. -/
theorem realPolynomial_circleIntegral_logDeriv_tendsto
    {ι : Type*} {phi : Filter ι} [phi.NeBot] [phi.IsCountablyGenerated]
    (A : ι → ℝ[X]) {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    (hA : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n w ↦ ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval w) f phi U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hzero : ∀ w ∈ U, f w ≠ 0)
    (c : ℂ) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hsphere : sphere c R ⊆ U) :
    Tendsto
      (fun n ↦ ∮ w in C(c, R),
        logDeriv (fun u ↦ ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval u) w) phi
      (nhds (∮ w in C(c, R), logDeriv f w)) := by
  exact tendsto_circleIntegral_logDeriv_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
    hA
    (Eventually.of_forall fun n ↦
      ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).differentiableOn)
    hU hzero c hR hsphere

/-- Real polynomial approximants to spectral xi have locally uniformly
convergent logarithmic derivatives on every zero-free open region. -/
theorem riemannXiSpectral_polynomial_logDeriv_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
    {ι : Type*} {phi : Filter ι} [phi.NeBot]
    (A : ι → ℝ[X]) {U : Set ℂ}
    (hA : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n w ↦ ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval w)
      riemannXiSpectral phi U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hzero : ∀ w ∈ U, riemannXiSpectral w ≠ 0) :
    TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n ↦ logDeriv
        (fun w ↦ ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval w))
      (logDeriv riemannXiSpectral) phi U :=
  realPolynomial_logDeriv_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn A hA hU hzero

/-- Spectral-xi specialization of convergence of logarithmic-derivative
circle integrals. -/
theorem riemannXiSpectral_polynomial_circleIntegral_logDeriv_tendsto
    {ι : Type*} {phi : Filter ι} [phi.NeBot] [phi.IsCountablyGenerated]
    (A : ι → ℝ[X]) {U : Set ℂ}
    (hA : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n w ↦ ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval w)
      riemannXiSpectral phi U)
    (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hzero : ∀ w ∈ U, riemannXiSpectral w ≠ 0)
    (c : ℂ) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hsphere : sphere c R ⊆ U) :
    Tendsto
      (fun n ↦ ∮ w in C(c, R),
        logDeriv (fun u ↦ ((A n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval u) w) phi
      (nhds (∮ w in C(c, R), logDeriv riemannXiSpectral w)) :=
  realPolynomial_circleIntegral_logDeriv_tendsto
    A hA hU hzero c hR hsphere

/-- Under failure of RH, the same exact root-pinned finite Hardy sequence has
logarithmic derivatives converging locally uniformly to `xi'/xi` on every
zero-free open region. -/
theorem exists_canonicalFiniteHardyFrontier_logDeriv_sequence_of_not_rh
    (hRH : ¬RiemannHypothesis) :
    ∃ eta : ℝ, 0 < eta ∧ ∃ z : ℂ, 0 < z.im ∧
      ∃ B : ℕ → ℝ[X],
        TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
          (fun n w ↦ ((B n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval w)
          riemannXiSpectral atTop Set.univ ∧
        (∀ n, CanonicalFiniteHardyFrontier (B n) eta z) ∧
        ∀ U : Set ℂ, IsOpen U →
          (∀ w ∈ U, riemannXiSpectral w ≠ 0) →
          TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
            (fun n ↦ logDeriv
              (fun w ↦ ((B n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval w))
            (logDeriv riemannXiSpectral) atTop U := by
  obtain ⟨eta, heta, z, hz, B, hB, hfrontier⟩ :=
    exists_canonicalFiniteHardyFrontier_sequence_of_not_rh hRH
  refine ⟨eta, heta, z, hz, B, hB, hfrontier, ?_⟩
  intro U hU hzero
  exact riemannXiSpectral_polynomial_logDeriv_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
    B (hB.mono (subset_univ U)) hU hzero

end

end RiemannGaussian

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.TaylorDerivativeCoefficient

/-!
# The Taylor coefficient of a differential monomial

A differential monomial in a power series `f` is a finite product of iterated formal
derivatives `∏ₜ f^{(jₜ)}`.  Its `N`-th Taylor coefficient is a weighted convolution over the
antidiagonal: for every splitting of `N` into per-factor degrees `lₜ`, the contribution is the
product of the shifted coefficients `coeff (lₜ + jₜ) f` each weighted by the rising factorial
`(lₜ+1)⋯(lₜ+jₜ)` supplied by the `jₜ`-th derivative
(`coeff_prod_iterate_derivative`).

This is the arithmetic core of generic ADE coefficient extraction: expanding a differential
polynomial `P(z, f, f', …, f^{(m)})` on the generic series and reading off the `z^N`
coefficient produces exactly such convolution sums, one per monomial of `P`.
-/

open PowerSeries Finset

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]

/-- **Differential-monomial coefficient.**  The `N`-th coefficient of a finite product of
iterated derivatives `∏ₜ f^{(jₜ)}` is the antidiagonal convolution of shifted coefficients,
each weighted by the rising factorial of its derivative order. -/
theorem coeff_prod_iterate_derivative {r : ℕ} (j : Fin r → ℕ) (f : R⟦X⟧) (N : ℕ) :
    coeff N (∏ t, (⇑(d⁄dX R))^[j t] f)
      = ∑ l ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r)).finsuppAntidiag N,
          ∏ t, coeff (l t + j t) f * ∏ i ∈ Finset.range (j t), ((l t + 1 + i : ℕ) : R) := by
  rw [PowerSeries.coeff_prod]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun l _ => ?_
  refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun t _ => ?_
  exact coeff_iterate_derivative f (j t) (l t)

end GaloisForLFunctions

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]

/-- **Monomial with a `z`-power factor.**  Prepending `X^a` to a differential monomial shifts
its coefficient index by `a`: the `N`-th coefficient of `X^a · ∏ₜ f^{(jₜ)}` reads the
differential-monomial convolution at index `N - a`, and vanishes for `N < a`. -/
theorem coeff_X_pow_mul_prod_iterate_derivative {r : ℕ} (a : ℕ) (j : Fin r → ℕ) (f : R⟦X⟧)
    (N : ℕ) :
    coeff N (X ^ a * ∏ t, (⇑(d⁄dX R))^[j t] f)
      = if a ≤ N then
          ∑ l ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r)).finsuppAntidiag (N - a),
            ∏ t, coeff (l t + j t) f * ∏ i ∈ Finset.range (j t), ((l t + 1 + i : ℕ) : R)
        else 0 := by
  rw [PowerSeries.coeff_X_pow_mul']
  split_ifs with h
  · rw [coeff_prod_iterate_derivative]
  · rfl

/-- **Source-sum constraint.**  Every convolution term contributing to the `N`-th coefficient
of a differential monomial `∏ₜ f^{(jₜ)}` reads original coefficients `a_{lₜ+jₜ}` whose indices
sum to `N + ∑ₜ jₜ` — the coefficient index plus the total derivative order.  This fixes the
source sum, the invariant on which the balanced-atom minimization operates. -/
theorem sum_source_index_of_mem_finsuppAntidiag {r N : ℕ} (j : Fin r → ℕ)
    {l : Fin r →₀ ℕ} (hl : l ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r)).finsuppAntidiag N) :
    ∑ t, (l t + j t) = N + ∑ t, j t := by
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  rw [Finset.mem_finsuppAntidiag] at hl
  rw [show (∑ t, l t) = ∑ t ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r)), l t from rfl, hl.1]

end GaloisForLFunctions

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]

/-- **Support of a differential monomial.**  If the `N`-th coefficient of `∏ₜ f^{(jₜ)}` is
nonzero, then there is a choice of source exponents `kₜ`, each in the support of `f`, summing
to `N + ∑ₜ jₜ` (the coefficient index plus the total derivative order).  Thus a differential
monomial reads only source exponents of `f`, and their sum is pinned — the input to the
gap-series balanced-atom argument for differential monomials. -/
theorem exists_source_of_coeff_prod_iterate_derivative_ne_zero {r : ℕ} (j : Fin r → ℕ)
    (f : R⟦X⟧) (N : ℕ)
    (h : coeff N (∏ t, (⇑(d⁄dX R))^[j t] f) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ k : Fin r → ℕ, (∀ t, coeff (k t) f ≠ 0) ∧ ∑ t, k t = N + ∑ t, j t := by
  rw [coeff_prod_iterate_derivative] at h
  obtain ⟨l, hl, hlne⟩ := Finset.exists_ne_zero_of_sum_ne_zero h
  refine ⟨fun t => l t + j t, fun t h0 => ?_, sum_source_index_of_mem_finsuppAntidiag j hl⟩
  exact hlne (Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ t) (by rw [h0, zero_mul]))

end GaloisForLFunctions

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.PositiveDensityQuantile
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gaussian.FourierTransform
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Deriv

/-!
# The literal positive two-Gaussian Fourier counterexample

The density is `exp (-x²) + exp (-2x²)`. Its actual logarithm is strictly
concave, while its entire literal Fourier integral has a non-real zero.
These facts require no finite-kernel-energy or spectral-reality premise.
-/

open MeasureTheory Set Complex

namespace RHTower.TwoGaussianComparison

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- The exact two-Gaussian density cited by the theta history card. -/
def density (x : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp (-x ^ 2) + Real.exp (-2 * x ^ 2)

theorem density_pos (x : ℝ) : 0 < density x := by
  unfold density
  positivity

theorem continuous_density : Continuous density := by
  unfold density
  fun_prop

theorem density_neg (x : ℝ) : density (-x) = density x := by
  simp [density]

theorem integrable_density : Integrable density := by
  have h₁ := integrable_exp_neg_mul_sq (b := 1) (by norm_num)
  have h₂ := integrable_exp_neg_mul_sq (b := 2) (by norm_num)
  apply (h₁.add h₂).congr
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by
    simp [density, Pi.add_apply]

/-- A genuine positive source, with the literal density and actual measure. -/
def source : PositiveDensitySource where
  k := density
  continuous_k := continuous_density
  pos_k := density_pos
  integrable_k := integrable_density

theorem source_mass : source.mass = Real.sqrt Real.pi + Real.sqrt (Real.pi / 2) := by
  change (∫ x : ℝ, density x) = _
  change (∫ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-x ^ 2) + Real.exp (-2 * x ^ 2)) = _
  rw [integral_add]
  · simpa using congrArg₂ (· + ·) (integral_gaussian 1) (integral_gaussian 2)
  · simpa using integrable_exp_neg_mul_sq (b := 1) (by norm_num)
  · exact integrable_exp_neg_mul_sq (b := 2) (by norm_num)

private def first (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (-2 * x) * Real.exp (-x ^ 2) + (-4 * x) * Real.exp (-2 * x ^ 2)

private def second (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (4 * x ^ 2 - 2) * Real.exp (-x ^ 2) +
    (16 * x ^ 2 - 4) * Real.exp (-2 * x ^ 2)

private theorem gaussian_one_hasDerivAt (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => Real.exp (-y ^ 2))
      ((-2 * x) * Real.exp (-x ^ 2)) x := by
  apply (((hasDerivAt_id x).pow 2).neg).exp.congr_deriv
  simp only [Pi.pow_apply, Pi.neg_apply, id_eq]
  ring

private theorem gaussian_two_hasDerivAt (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => Real.exp (-2 * y ^ 2))
      ((-4 * x) * Real.exp (-2 * x ^ 2)) x := by
  apply (((hasDerivAt_id x).pow 2).const_mul (-2)).exp.congr_deriv
  simp only [Pi.pow_apply, id_eq]
  ring

private theorem density_hasDerivAt (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt density (first x) x :=
  (gaussian_one_hasDerivAt x).add (gaussian_two_hasDerivAt x)

private theorem first_hasDerivAt (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt first (second x) x := by
  have h₁ := ((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul (-2)).mul (gaussian_one_hasDerivAt x)
  have h₂ := ((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul (-4)).mul (gaussian_two_hasDerivAt x)
  apply (h₁.add h₂).congr_deriv
  simp only [second, id_eq]
  ring

private theorem curvature_pos (x : ℝ) : 0 < first x ^ 2 - density x * second x := by
  let u : ℝ := x ^ 2
  let g : ℝ := Real.exp (-u)
  have hu : 0 ≤ u := sq_nonneg x
  have hg : 0 < g := Real.exp_pos _
  have hh := Real.add_one_le_exp (u / 2)
  have hp := Real.exp_pos (u / 2)
  have hexp : Real.exp u = Real.exp (u / 2) ^ 2 := by
    rw [pow_two, ← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have hbound : 2 * u ≤ Real.exp u := by
    rw [hexp]
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (u / 2 - 1)]
  have hcancel : Real.exp u * g = 1 := by
    dsimp [g]
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    simp
  have hprod : 2 * u * g ≤ 1 := by
    have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hbound hg.le
    rwa [hcancel] at h
  have hbracket : 0 < 1 + (3 - 2 * u) * g + 2 * g ^ 2 := by
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg g]
  have h₂ : Real.exp (-2 * x ^ 2) = g ^ 2 := by
    change Real.exp (-2 * x ^ 2) = Real.exp (-x ^ 2) ^ 2
    rw [pow_two (Real.exp (-x ^ 2)), ← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have hid : first x ^ 2 - density x * second x =
      2 * g ^ 2 * (1 + (3 - 2 * u) * g + 2 * g ^ 2) := by
    dsimp [first, density, second, u]
    rw [h₂]
    change ((-2 * x) * g + (-4 * x) * g ^ 2) ^ 2 -
      (g + g ^ 2) * ((4 * x ^ 2 - 2) * g + (16 * x ^ 2 - 4) * g ^ 2) = _
    ring
  rw [hid]
  positivity

private theorem deriv_log_density (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun y => Real.log (density y)) x = first x / density x :=
  ((density_hasDerivAt x).log (density_pos x).ne').deriv

private theorem deriv_log_density_two (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (deriv (fun y => Real.log (density y))) x =
      (density x * second x - first x ^ 2) / density x ^ 2 := by
  have hfirst : deriv (fun y => Real.log (density y)) =
      fun y => first y / density y := funext deriv_log_density
  rw [hfirst]
  calc
    deriv (fun y => first y / density y) x =
        (second x * density x - first x * first x) / density x ^ 2 :=
      ((first_hasDerivAt x).div (density_hasDerivAt x) (density_pos x).ne').deriv
    _ = _ := by ring

theorem deriv_log_density_two_neg (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (deriv (fun y => Real.log (density y))) x < 0 := by
  rw [deriv_log_density_two]
  exact div_neg_of_neg_of_pos (by linarith [curvature_pos x])
    (pow_pos (density_pos x) 2)

/-- Strict log-concavity is a theorem of the actual literal logarithm. -/
theorem strictConcaveOn_log_density :
    StrictConcaveOn ℝ univ (fun x => Real.log (density x)) := by
  apply strictConcaveOn_univ_of_deriv2_neg
    (continuous_density.log fun x => (density_pos x).ne')
  intro x
  simpa only [Function.iterate_succ_apply, Function.iterate_zero_apply] using
    deriv_log_density_two_neg x

private theorem gaussian_integrand (b : ℝ) (z : ℂ) (x : ℝ) :
    Complex.exp (I * z * x) * (Real.exp (-b * x ^ 2) : ℂ) =
      Complex.exp (-(b : ℂ) * (x : ℂ) ^ 2 + (I * z) * x + 0) := by
  rw [Complex.ofReal_exp, ← Complex.exp_add]
  congr 1
  push_cast
  ring

private theorem integrable_fourierGaussian {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (z : ℂ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Complex.exp (I * z * x) *
      (Real.exp (-b * x ^ 2) : ℂ)) := by
  have h := integrable_cexp_quadratic (b := (b : ℂ)) (by simpa using hb) (I * z) 0
  exact h.congr (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => (gaussian_integrand b z x).symm)

private theorem fourierGaussian_integral {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (z : ℂ) :
    (∫ x : ℝ, Complex.exp (I * z * x) * (Real.exp (-b * x ^ 2) : ℂ)) =
      (Real.sqrt (Real.pi / b) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (-z ^ 2 / (4 * (b : ℂ))) := by
  have h := integral_cexp_quadratic (b := -(b : ℂ)) (by simpa using hb) (I * z) 0
  have hexponent : (0 : ℂ) - (I * z) ^ 2 / (4 * -(b : ℂ)) =
      -z ^ 2 / (4 * (b : ℂ)) := by
    rw [mul_pow, Complex.I_sq]
    simp
    ring
  have hpower : ((Real.pi : ℂ) / (b : ℂ)) ^ (1 / 2 : ℂ) =
      (Real.sqrt (Real.pi / b) : ℂ) := by
    rw [← Complex.ofReal_div, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]
    convert (Complex.ofReal_cpow (div_pos Real.pi_pos hb).le (1 / 2 : ℝ)).symm
      using 1
    norm_num
  rw [neg_neg, hexponent, hpower] at h
  rw [← h]
  apply integral_congr_ae
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall (gaussian_integrand b z)

/-- The physical complex-frequency transform of the literal source. -/
def transform (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∫ x : ℝ, Complex.exp (I * z * x) * (source.k x : ℂ)

/-- The entire closed formula with its exact Gaussian mass constants. -/
def closedForm (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  (Real.sqrt Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.exp (-z ^ 2 / 4) +
    (Real.sqrt (Real.pi / 2) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (-z ^ 2 / 8)

theorem integrable_transform (z : ℂ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Complex.exp (I * z * x) * (source.k x : ℂ)) := by
  have h₁ := integrable_fourierGaussian (b := 1) (by norm_num) z
  have h₂ := integrable_fourierGaussian (b := 2) (by norm_num) z
  apply (h₁.add h₂).congr
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by
    simp [source, density, mul_add, Pi.add_apply]

/-- Exact literal Fourier integration at every complex frequency. -/
theorem transform_eq (z : ℂ) : transform z = closedForm z := by
  unfold transform closedForm
  change (∫ x : ℝ, Complex.exp (I * z * x) * (density x : ℂ)) = _
  simp only [density, Complex.ofReal_add, mul_add]
  rw [integral_add]
  · simpa [show (4 : ℂ) * 2 = 8 by norm_num] using congrArg₂ (· + ·)
      (fourierGaussian_integral (b := 1) (by norm_num) z)
      (fourierGaussian_integral (b := 2) (by norm_num) z)
  · simpa using integrable_fourierGaussian (b := 1) (by norm_num) z
  · exact integrable_fourierGaussian (b := 2) (by norm_num) z

theorem differentiable_transform : Differentiable ℂ transform := by
  have heq : transform = closedForm := funext transform_eq
  rw [heq]
  unfold closedForm
  fun_prop

/-- The actual transform is strictly positive on the whole real line. -/
theorem transform_real_re_pos (t : ℝ) : 0 < (transform (t : ℂ)).re := by
  rw [transform_eq]
  have h₁ : -(t : ℂ) ^ 2 / 4 = ((-t ^ 2 / 4 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
    push_cast
    rfl
  have h₂ : -(t : ℂ) ^ 2 / 8 = ((-t ^ 2 / 8 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
    push_cast
    rfl
  simp only [closedForm, h₁, h₂, Complex.add_re, Complex.mul_re,
    Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, zero_mul, sub_zero, Complex.exp_ofReal_re]
  have hA : 0 < Real.sqrt Real.pi := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr Real.pi_pos
  have hB : 0 < Real.sqrt (Real.pi / 2) := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (by positivity)
  positivity

theorem transform_real_ne_zero (t : ℝ) : transform (t : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  have hp := transform_real_re_pos t
  rw [h] at hp
  norm_num at hp

/-- The square of a constructed non-real zero, using only the exact mass ratio. -/
def zeroSquare : ℂ :=
  -8 * ((Real.log (Real.sqrt (Real.pi / 2) / Real.sqrt Real.pi) : ℂ) +
    (Real.pi : ℂ) * I)

/-- An explicit principal half-power of the source-derived square. -/
def offRealZero : ℂ := zeroSquare ^ (1 / 2 : ℂ)

theorem offRealZero_sq : offRealZero ^ 2 = zeroSquare := by
  unfold offRealZero
  rw [← Complex.cpow_mul_nat]
  norm_num

theorem offRealZero_im_ne_zero : offRealZero.im ≠ 0 := by
  intro hz
  have h := congrArg Complex.im offRealZero_sq
  have hsquare : zeroSquare.im = -8 * Real.pi := by
    simp [zeroSquare, Complex.mul_im]
  rw [hsquare, pow_two, Complex.mul_im, hz] at h
  simp only [mul_zero, zero_mul, add_zero] at h
  linarith [Real.pi_pos]

private theorem exp_offRealZero :
    Complex.exp (-offRealZero ^ 2 / 8) =
      -((Real.sqrt (Real.pi / 2) / Real.sqrt Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  rw [offRealZero_sq]
  have harg : -zeroSquare / 8 =
      (Real.log (Real.sqrt (Real.pi / 2) / Real.sqrt Real.pi) : ℂ) +
        (Real.pi : ℂ) * I := by
    unfold zeroSquare
    ring
  rw [harg, Complex.exp_add_pi_mul_I, ← Complex.ofReal_exp]
  rw [Real.exp_log (div_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (by positivity))
    (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr Real.pi_pos))]

/-- The constructed non-real point is a zero of the actual Lebesgue integral. -/
theorem transform_offRealZero : transform offRealZero = 0 := by
  have hd : Complex.exp (-offRealZero ^ 2 / 4) =
      Complex.exp (-offRealZero ^ 2 / 8) ^ 2 := by
    rw [pow_two (Complex.exp (-offRealZero ^ 2 / 8)), ← Complex.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  rw [transform_eq]
  unfold closedForm
  rw [hd, exp_offRealZero]
  push_cast
  field_simp [Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr Real.pi_pos).ne']
  ring

/-- Positive even strict log-concavity coexists with a literal off-real Fourier zero. -/
theorem source_counterexample :
    (∀ x : ℝ, source.k (-x) = source.k x) ∧
      StrictConcaveOn ℝ univ (fun x => Real.log (source.k x)) ∧
      (∀ t : ℝ, (transform (t : ℂ)).re > 0) ∧
      ∃ z : ℂ, z.im ≠ 0 ∧ transform z = 0 :=
  ⟨density_neg, strictConcaveOn_log_density, transform_real_re_pos,
    offRealZero, offRealZero_im_ne_zero, transform_offRealZero⟩

end
end RHTower.TwoGaussianComparison

```lean
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.TwoGaussianSourceCounterexample
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Hedenmalm.HedenmalmQuantileNormalForm
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.HermiteGaussianEnvelope
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Polynomial
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.IteratedDeriv.Lemmas
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntegralEqImproper

/-!
# Every literal derivative of the two-Gaussian source

Polynomial envelopes prove admission to the ORIGINAL reciprocal-density source
space at every order. The actual pinned primitive kills the source and lowers
each ordinary derivative. No finite kernel energy or bounded inverse is assumed.
-/

open MeasureTheory Filter Set GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
open RHTower.HedenmalmQuantile
open scoped Topology ENNReal

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower.TwoGaussianComparison

attribute [local instance 2000] Real.measurableSpace
attribute [local instance 2000] NormedSpace.complexToReal

private abbrev μS := volume.withDensity (realDensity (sourceWeight source))

local instance : Fact ((2 : ENNReal) ≠ ⊤) := ⟨by norm_num⟩

/-- The exact polynomial recurrence for ordinary Gaussian derivatives. -/
def derivativePolynomial (b : ℝ) : ℕ → Polynomial ℝ
  | 0 => 1
  | n + 1 => (derivativePolynomial b n).derivative -
      Polynomial.C (2 * b) * Polynomial.X * derivativePolynomial b n

/-- An explicit polynomial envelope, identified below with the ordinary derivative. -/
def gaussianDerivative (b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (derivativePolynomial b n).eval x * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2))

theorem continuous_gaussianDerivative (b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    Continuous (gaussianDerivative b n) := by
  unfold gaussianDerivative
  fun_prop

theorem hasDerivAt_gaussianDerivative (b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (gaussianDerivative b n) (gaussianDerivative b (n + 1) x) x := by
  have hp := (derivativePolynomial b n).hasDerivAt x
  have hg := (((hasDerivAt_id x).pow 2).const_mul b).neg.exp
  apply (hp.mul hg).congr_deriv
  simp only [gaussianDerivative, derivativePolynomial, Polynomial.eval_sub,
    Polynomial.eval_mul, Polynomial.eval_C, Polynomial.eval_X,
    Pi.neg_apply, Pi.pow_apply, id_eq]
  ring

theorem iteratedDeriv_gaussian (b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    iteratedDeriv n (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2))) =
      gaussianDerivative b n := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      funext x
      simp [iteratedDeriv_zero, gaussianDerivative, derivativePolynomial]
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [iteratedDeriv_succ, ih]
      funext x
      exact (hasDerivAt_gaussianDerivative b n x).deriv

theorem iteratedDeriv_density (n : ℕ) :
    iteratedDeriv n density =
      fun x => gaussianDerivative 1 n x + gaussianDerivative 2 n x := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      funext x
      simp [iteratedDeriv_zero, gaussianDerivative, derivativePolynomial, density]
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [iteratedDeriv_succ, ih]
      funext x
      exact ((hasDerivAt_gaussianDerivative 1 n x).add
        (hasDerivAt_gaussianDerivative 2 n x)).deriv

/-- The actual ordinary derivative of the literal source, in complex coordinates. -/
def derivativeFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  (iteratedDeriv n density x : ℝ)

theorem derivativeFunction_eq (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    derivativeFunction n x =
      ((gaussianDerivative 1 n x + gaussianDerivative 2 n x : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  rw [derivativeFunction, iteratedDeriv_density]

private theorem derivativeFunction_eq_fun (n : ℕ) :
    derivativeFunction n = fun x : ℝ =>
      ((gaussianDerivative 1 n x + gaussianDerivative 2 n x : ℝ) : ℂ) :=
  funext (derivativeFunction_eq n)

theorem derivativeFunction_zero (x : ℝ) :
    derivativeFunction 0 x = (source.k x : ℂ) := by
  simp [derivativeFunction, iteratedDeriv_zero, source]

theorem continuous_derivativeFunction (n : ℕ) :
    Continuous (derivativeFunction n) := by
  have h := Complex.continuous_ofReal.comp
    ((continuous_gaussianDerivative 1 n).add (continuous_gaussianDerivative 2 n))
  rw [derivativeFunction_eq_fun]
  exact h

theorem hasDerivAt_derivativeFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (derivativeFunction n) (derivativeFunction (n + 1) x) x := by
  have h := ((hasDerivAt_gaussianDerivative 1 n x).add
    (hasDerivAt_gaussianDerivative 2 n x)).ofReal_comp
  rw [derivativeFunction_eq_fun, derivativeFunction_eq]
  exact h

private theorem integrable_gaussianDerivative {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (gaussianDerivative b n) :=
  integrable_polyEval_mul_gauss (derivativePolynomial b n) hb

theorem integrable_derivativeFunction (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (derivativeFunction n) := by
  have h : Integrable (fun x : ℝ =>
      ((gaussianDerivative 1 n x + gaussianDerivative 2 n x : ℝ) : ℂ)) :=
    ((integrable_gaussianDerivative (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1) n).add
      (integrable_gaussianDerivative (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 2) n)).ofReal
  rw [derivativeFunction_eq_fun]
  exact h

theorem derivativeFunction_tendsto_atBot (n : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (derivativeFunction n) atBot (𝓝 0) := by
  have h₁ := tendsto_polyEval_mul_gauss_atBot (derivativePolynomial 1 n)
    (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1)
  have h₂ := tendsto_polyEval_mul_gauss_atBot (derivativePolynomial 2 n)
    (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 2)
  have hr : Tendsto (fun x => gaussianDerivative 1 n x + gaussianDerivative 2 n x)
      atBot (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa only [gaussianDerivative, add_zero] using h₁.add h₂
  have h := (Complex.continuous_ofReal.tendsto 0).comp hr
  rw [derivativeFunction_eq_fun]
  convert h using 1 <;> rfl

theorem derivativeFunction_tendsto_atTop (n : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (derivativeFunction n) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  have h₁ := tendsto_polyEval_mul_gauss_atTop (derivativePolynomial 1 n)
    (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1)
  have h₂ := tendsto_polyEval_mul_gauss_atTop (derivativePolynomial 2 n)
    (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 2)
  have hr : Tendsto (fun x => gaussianDerivative 1 n x + gaussianDerivative 2 n x)
      atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa only [gaussianDerivative, add_zero] using h₁.add h₂
  have h := (Complex.continuous_ofReal.tendsto 0).comp hr
  rw [derivativeFunction_eq_fun]
  convert h using 1 <;> rfl

theorem integral_derivativeFunction_succ (n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x, derivativeFunction (n + 1) x) = 0 :=
  integral_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrable (hasDerivAt_derivativeFunction n)
    (integrable_derivativeFunction (n + 1)) (integrable_derivativeFunction n)

theorem integral_Iic_derivativeFunction_succ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    (∫ y in Iic x, derivativeFunction (n + 1) y) = derivativeFunction n x := by
  simpa using integral_Iic_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto'
    (fun y _ => hasDerivAt_derivativeFunction n y)
    (integrable_derivativeFunction (n + 1)).integrableOn
    (derivativeFunction_tendsto_atBot n)

theorem sourceInverse_derivativeFunction_zero (x : ℝ) :
    sourceInverse source (derivativeFunction 0) x = 0 := by
  rw [sourceInverse]
  simp_rw [derivativeFunction_zero]
  rw [integral_complex_ofReal]
  change Complex.I * (∫ y in Iic x,
    ((source.k y : ℂ) - ((source.mass : ℂ) / (source.mass : ℂ)) * (source.k y : ℂ))) = 0
  have hM : (source.mass : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast source.mass_ne_zero
  rw [div_self hM]
  simp

theorem sourceInverse_derivativeFunction_succ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    sourceInverse source (derivativeFunction (n + 1)) x =
      Complex.I * derivativeFunction n x := by
  rw [sourceInverse, integral_derivativeFunction_succ]
  simp only [zero_div, zero_mul, sub_zero]
  rw [integral_Iic_derivativeFunction_succ]

private theorem polynomial_gaussian_memLp (p : Polynomial ℝ) {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b)
    (hdom : ∀ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2)) ≤ source.k x) :
    MemLp (fun x : ℝ => ((p.eval x * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ)) 2 μS := by
  have hc : Continuous (fun x : ℝ =>
      ((p.eval x * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by fun_prop
  have hm := (measurable_sqrtWeight (measurable_sourceWeight source)).aestronglyMeasurable.mul
    (hc.aestronglyMeasurable (μ := volume))
  apply (memLp_two_withDensity_iff (measurable_sourceWeight source)
    (sourceWeight_pos source)).mpr
  apply (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm hm).mpr
  refine (integrable_polyEval_mul_gauss (p ^ 2) hb).mono' (hm.norm.pow 2) ?_
  filter_upwards with x
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
  have hs : ‖sqrtWeight (sourceWeight source) x *
      ((p.eval x * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ^ 2 =
      (source.k x)⁻¹ * (p.eval x * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2))) ^ 2 := by
    rw [norm_mul, mul_pow, sqrtWeight, Complex.norm_real, Complex.norm_real,
      Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs, sq_abs,
      Real.sq_sqrt (sourceWeight_pos source x).le]
    rfl
  change ‖sqrtWeight (sourceWeight source) x *
    ((p.eval x * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ^ 2 ≤
    (p ^ 2).eval x * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2))
  rw [hs, Polynomial.eval_pow]
  have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hdom x)
    (mul_nonneg (sq_nonneg (p.eval x)) (Real.exp_pos (-(b * x ^ 2))).le)
  have hdiv : (p.eval x * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2))) ^ 2 / source.k x ≤
      p.eval x ^ 2 * Real.exp (-(b * x ^ 2)) := by
    apply (div_le_iff₀ (source.pos_k x)).mpr
    convert h using 1
    ring
  simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm] using hdiv

/-- EVERY actual derivative belongs to ORIGINAL reciprocal-density L². -/
theorem derivativeFunction_memLp (n : ℕ) : MemLp (derivativeFunction n) 2 μS := by
  have h₁ := polynomial_gaussian_memLp (derivativePolynomial 1 n)
    (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1) (fun x => by
      change Real.exp (-(1 * x ^ 2)) ≤ density x
      dsimp [density]
      have hp := Real.exp_pos (-2 * x ^ 2)
      simp only [one_mul]
      linarith)
  have h₂ := polynomial_gaussian_memLp (derivativePolynomial 2 n)
    (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 2) (fun x => by
      change Real.exp (-(2 * x ^ 2)) ≤ density x
      dsimp [density]
      have hp := Real.exp_pos (-x ^ 2)
      have he : -(2 * x ^ 2) = -2 * x ^ 2 := by ring
      rw [he]
      linarith)
  refine MemLp.ae_eq ?_ (h₁.add h₂)
  filter_upwards with x
  simp only [Pi.add_apply, derivativeFunction_eq, gaussianDerivative, Complex.ofReal_add]

/-- Genuine source vectors of the admitted ordinary derivatives. -/
def sourceDerivativeVector (n : ℕ) : SourceSpace source :=
  (derivativeFunction_memLp n).toLp (derivativeFunction n)

theorem sourceDerivativeVector_coe (n : ℕ) :
    sourceDerivativeVector n =ᵐ[μS] derivativeFunction n :=
  MemLp.coeFn_toLp _

end RHTower.TwoGaussianComparison
```
